Threat actor|An individual or group that poses a risk to the confidentiality, integrity or availability of an organisation's systems or data — e.g. nation-state, criminal, hacktivist or insider.|intel,cyber,threats
APT|Advanced Persistent Threat: a sophisticated, well-resourced adversary that maintains long-term, stealthy access to a network, typically for espionage or data theft.|threats,intel
TTP|Tactics, Techniques and Procedures: the observable behaviour of an adversary, from high-level goals (tactics) to specific actions (techniques) and tools (procedures).|intel,frameworks
MITRE ATT&CK|A globally accessible knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques built from real-world observations — used to model, detect and defend against threats.|frameworks
Indicator of Compromise (IOC)|Forensic evidence — such as a file hash, IP address, domain or registry key — that suggests a system or network has been compromised.|intel,detection
Zero-day vulnerability|A security flaw unknown to the vendor and without a patch, which attackers can exploit before a fix is available.|vulnerability
Phishing|A social engineering attack using spoofed communications (usually email) to trick a victim into revealing credentials or installing malware.|social engineering
Spear phishing|A targeted form of phishing aimed at a specific individual or organisation, often using personal detail to appear legitimate.|social engineering
Ransomware|Malware that encrypts a victim's files and demands a payment (ransom) in exchange for decryption.|malware
SOC|Security Operations Centre: the team that monitors, detects, analyses and responds to an organisation's cyber threats, often around the clock.|defence
SIEM|Security Information and Event Management: centralises and analyses security logs and alerts from across the network for detection and incident response.|defence
EDR|Endpoint Detection and Response: security tooling that continuously monitors endpoints (laptops, servers, mobile) for malicious activity and enables response.|defence
IDS vs IPS|An Intrusion Detection System monitors and alerts on suspicious activity; an Intrusion Prevention System also sits in line and actively blocks it.|defence
CIA triad|Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability — the three core objectives of information security.|foundations
Defence in depth|Layering multiple, overlapping security controls so that if one control fails, others still protect the asset.|foundations
MFA|Multi-Factor Authentication: requiring two or more distinct evidence factors (something you know, have, or are) before granting access.|foundations
DDoS|Distributed Denial of Service: overwhelming a target with traffic from many compromised sources to make it unavailable.|attacks
Malware|Malicious software — such as viruses, worms, trojans, spyware and ransomware — designed to harm or exploit a system.|malware
CVE|Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures: a public, standardised identifier and catalogue for known cybersecurity vulnerabilities.|vulnerability
Vulnerability|A weakness in a system or process that a threat can exploit to compromise confidentiality, integrity or availability.|vulnerability
Man-in-the-Middle (MITM)|An attack in which the adversary secretly relays and possibly alters communication between two parties who believe they are talking directly.|attacks
SQL injection|Injecting malicious SQL into a query to manipulate a back-end database — to read, modify or delete data.|web security
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)|Injecting client-side scripts into web pages that are then executed by other users' browsers.|web security
OSINT|Open Source Intelligence: intelligence derived from publicly available sources such as news, social media and public records.|intel,collection
HUMINT|Human Intelligence: intelligence gathered from human sources rather than technical means.|intel,collection
SIGINT|Signals Intelligence: intelligence gathered from intercepted signals and communications.|intel,collection
Symmetric vs asymmetric encryption|Symmetric uses a single shared key for both encryption and decryption (e.g. AES); asymmetric uses a matched public/private key pair (e.g. RSA, ECC).|crypto
Hashing|A one-way function that maps data to a fixed-size digest; used to verify integrity, and not intended to be reversed.|crypto

Essential Eight|The Australian Cyber Security Centre's prioritised list of eight mitigation strategies (patch apps and OS, MFA, application control, restrict admin privileges, and more).|australia,frameworks
Threat intelligence|Evidence-based knowledge about existing or emerging threats, used to inform decisions on preventing, detecting and responding to attacks.|intel
Cyber kill chain|A model describing the stages of an attack: reconnaissance, weaponisation, delivery, exploitation, installation, command and control, and actions on objectives.|frameworks
Lateral movement|The techniques an adversary uses to move across a network to reach higher-value systems and data.|intel,attacks
Privilege escalation|Gaining a higher level of access or permission than was originally granted.|attacks
Data exfiltration|The unauthorised transfer of data out of a network or system.|attacks
Purple team|A collaborative security exercise in which red (offensive) and blue (defensive) teams work together to improve detection and response.|defence
Incident response lifecycle|The phases of handling an incident: preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident lessons learned.|defence,incident response
PII|Personally Identifiable Information: data that can be used to identify an individual, such as name, email, ID number or date of birth.|privacy
SOC 2|An auditing / attestation framework for service organisations covering security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy controls.|compliance
